newsitem.title: CHINA: China urges Taiwan to act to improve relations.
newsitem.headline: China urges Taiwan to act to improve relations.

text.p: China on Thursday brushed aside a U.S. call not to hold military exercises on the eve of Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule and urged rival Taiwan to take more actions conducive to improving relations.

Asked whether China planned to hold military exercises in the weeks before the handover of Hong Kong on July 1, at the same time as planned Taiwan war games, Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai declined to comment.
He side-stepped a question on Taiwan's military exercises planned for June 23-24 but urged the island, which it considers a rebel province, to boost strained ties between the two rivals.
"We hope the Taiwan authorities will take more actions that are conducive to improving relations between the two sides," he told a regular news briefing.
He also avoided comment on a U.S. call on China and Taiwan not to stage military exercises during the sensitive run-up to Hong Kong's return to Chinese control.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese sovereignty on July 1 after 156 years as a British colony.
Beijing has regarded Taiwan a renegade province since Nationalist troops lost a civil war and took refuge on the island in 1949.
China says its handling of Hong Kong's return under a "one country, two systems" model of political and economic autonomy should reassure Taiwan of its own future with the mainland.

In Taipei, a defence ministry spokesman said Taiwan had no plans to cancel what it called routine military drills on the eve of Hong Kong's handover to China despite a U.S. request not to hold the exercises.
"This is a routine annual exercise. We will proceed," a defence ministry spokesman told Reuters.

Taiwan has said its planned exercises are unrelated to the Hong Kong handover despite the sensitive timing, but the spokesman confirmed the large-scale war games were intended to boost public confidence.
"You shouldn't link this too much to the (reported) Chinese communists' manoeuvres," the spokesman said. "This is not a military competition with the Chinese communists."
An independent Hong Kong newspaper has said China plans to respond to Taiwan's war games with its own military exercises this month.
China held war games and missile tests near Taiwan in the run-up to the island's first direct presidential election in March 1996 to warn voters against a move towards independence.
Washington responded by sending two aircraft carrier battle groups to the region in a show of support for Taiwan.
China has threatened to invade if Taiwan declares independence.
